title: QUIC RFC 9000 Server Connection ID Adoption And Continuity Verification
verification_method: Focused S7P2 requirement-home tests, affected CRT compatibility tests, Release build, regenerated QUIC coverage triage, SpecTrace JSON validation, and whitespace diff checking.
scope: This verification covers RFC 9000 Section 7.2 server Source Connection ID adoption and conflicting-source continuity during connection establishment, plus the server first-client-Initial Destination Connection ID derivation and the NEW_CONNECTION_ID-only later-change boundary.
expected_result: The requirement-home tests show that the client adopts the first server Initial or Retry Source Connection ID for subsequent sends, keeps a Retry-selected outbound Destination Connection ID when the first post-Retry server Initial carries a different server Source Connection ID, keeps 0-RTT formatting aligned with the adopted server Source Connection ID after server Initial receipt, refuses later Initial or Handshake source changes after the first valid server Initial, refuses later Retry source changes, and keeps later Destination Connection ID changes limited to NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames. The server proof shows Initial responses use the Source Connection ID from the first received client Initial rather than the client's Original Destination Connection ID.
procedure: Run the focused S7P2 0009 through 0014 requirement-home filter.
Run the affected CRT/S5P2P1/S12P2 compatibility filter that explicitly opts into replacement peer Initial behavior.
Run the broader S7P2 requirement-home filter with --no-build.
Check the resulting diff for whitespace errors.
preconditions: The client runtime has configured Initial packet protection and the bootstrap outbound path.
The server handshake proof uses the first client Initial generated by the runtime helper.
The CRT replacement peer Initial behavior is enabled only through an explicit internal opt-in and is not the default RFC path.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This verification does not claim preferred-address migration, server-address-change policy, public API widening, general multi-attempt handshake orchestration, hosted interop readiness, or full connection-ID lifecycle parity beyond the Section 7.2 adoption and conflicting-source floor.

status_summary: Passed locally on 2026-05-05. The focused S7P2 0009 through 0014 requirement-home filter passed 19/19, the affected CRT/S5P2P1/S12P2 compatibility filter passed 7/7, the retry-harness regression filter passed 5/5, the Release build passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors, the broader S7P2 no-build filter passed 38/38, the full Release no-build suite passed 4,377/4,377, regenerated QUIC coverage triage marks S7P2 0009 through 0014 trace_clean, SpecTrace core validation passed across 418 JSON artifacts, and git diff --check passed.
